instruction: Complete each requested subpart within the existing length bounds. Include the requested precision, dates, speaker corrections and provenance when the passages supply them. Do not replace a supported requested detail with an unrelated limitation. Do not repeat a user's quoted label or put proposed application field values in quotation marks. State replacements and corrections in ordinary unquoted prose. Use no quotation marks around isolated terms; paraphrase instead. Distinguish the author's stated duty or strategic advice from an example or prediction about what might happen in a future crisis; an illustrative prediction alone may not answer a question about the full advice. Keep each action, cause, consequence and location in a reconstructed story within the author's explicit reported or hypothetical scope. A general inability to settle an outcome does not license a newly invented death-or-survival story or a claim that the author explicitly admitted a particular uncertainty. State only the bounded limitation the source supports. For local estimates, identify which population a percentage describes and the missing local composition, task and adoption information, without inventing a local outcome. Check that the final answer covers all requested parts before ending.
